entityDescription:
Kontron Transportation is a leading global supplier of end-to-end communication solutions for mission-critical networks. Our core customers are railways across Europe and beyond. We specialize in systems that produce, transport, and process voice, data, and video — reliably, securely, sustainably, and efficiently.
Our solutions include GSM-Railways, FRMCS (Future Railway Mobile Communication Systems), and MCx (mission-critical over public networks) with IWF (interworking functions). We also offer enhanced radio solutions, radio access networks for 4G/5G private networks, transmission networks, and cybersecurity solutions. In addition, our portfolio includes communication products for Secondary Lines and other mission-critical network operators. We also provide mobility products like validators and fare collection systems for public transport operators.
For over 25 years, we have been fully dedicated to railways. Today, we continue to drive the evolution of broadband solutions for mission-critical networks, for instance as an associated member of Europe’s Rail Joint Undertaking (EU-Rail), making us the perfect partner for FRMCS.

Company description: Company Profile
We are a specialized company focused on the design and development of advanced remote sensing systems and solutions, with particular expertise in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technologies and the processing and analysis of satellite and ground-based radar data.
Our activities combine expertise in systems engineering, signal processing, algorithm development, and geospatial data analysis, with the goal of transforming complex remote sensing data into reliable and actionable information for scientific, industrial, environmental, and Earth observation applications.
Our core expertise includes:
- Design of SAR remote sensing systems, from requirements definition to system architecture and technology development;
- Definition and development of advanced algorithms for SAR data processing, focusing on signal processing, image analysis, feature extraction, and information retrieval;
- SAR-based soil moisture estimation and monitoring, including the development of algorithms and processing methodologies for the retrieval of soil moisture from radar observations, supporting applications in agriculture, hydrology, environmental monitoring, and land surface characterization;
- GNSS/GPS reflectometry (GNSS-R) techniques for the monitoring and characterization of the Earth's surface and environmental parameters;
- Differential SAR Interferometry (DInSAR) for the detection and monitoring of ground and infrastructure deformation, enabling measurements at millimetric scale;
- Development of dedicated software, processing chains, and analytical methods for the automated processing, integration, and interpretation of remote sensing data.
Our expertise covers the entire processing chain, from raw sensor data to high-level geophysical information, with a strong focus on developing innovative algorithms and tailored solutions for challenging remote sensing applications.
As a small and highly specialized company, we offer a flexible, agile, and strongly innovation-driven approach, allowing us to work closely with research institutions

description:
InnoviGuard AB doesn't ask you to trust your data and your commands. It proves them.

We build P55 Nexus, a proof engine for space communications. A satellite can go long stretches without contact with the ground. Most security models assume that connection is always there: a certificate authority reachable, a revocation list current, a key rotation schedule kept. P55 Nexus does not depend on any of that. It lets a satellite prove that a command came from mission control, and lets mission control prove that data came from the satellite, using proof that stands on its own.

Each proof is bound to the specific hardware that produced it. Nothing captured from one system can be reused to impersonate another. Ground stations, satellites, and the links between them are proven independently, with no shared infrastructure to fail or be compromised.

InnoviGuard develops this technology and applies it across the space communications chain: ground segment, uplink command authentication, inter-satellite links. We are currently engaged in an ESA BIC Sweden project. InnoviGuard was founded by Carl Hendrix, who brings close to 30 years of experience in security.

P55 Nexus is designed to complement existing CCSDS standards rather than replace them. SDLS secures the link layer; P55 Nexus operates at the space packet level, adding proof of origin and destination that SDLS's frame-level protection does not address. The two coexist in the same stack.
entityDescription:
Every day, critical data moves between systems that don't fully trust each other. A command reaches a satellite. A model reaches an edge device. A sample reaches a lab. Each time, there's a moment of doubt: is this really what it claims to be, from who it claims, unchanged along the way?
InnoviGuard AB, a Swedish deep-tech company, built P55 Nexus to close that gap. Proof, not permission. It's already at work today: authenticating biodiversity data collected in the field, and confirming AI models reaching space-edge devices are genuine and untouched. InnoviGuard is part of ESA BIC Sweden, bringing this to satellite command and control, working with partners in edge AI for space and satellite-based ocean surveillance.
We don't ask anyone to trust us. We give them proof.
Founded and led by Carl Hendrix, InnoviGuard is based at Ideon Science Park, Lund.

entityDescription:
The Sanitary Engineering Laboratory (SEL) operates within the Department of Water Resources and Environmental Engineering of the School of Civil Engineering at the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA). As one of Greece’s foremost research and education centres in the fields of water resources management and environmental protection, SEL combines academic excellence with real-world impact, fostering innovation and developing smart, sustainable solutions to contemporary environmental challenges.
Its activities encompass both fundamental and applied interdisciplinary research in water resources management, drinking water treatment, wastewater and sludge treatment, solid waste management, bioremediation, water and sludge reuse, nutrient and energy recovery from waste, mathematical modelling of biological processes, aquatic environment quality assessment, the fate of priority pollutants and emerging contaminants in aquatic environments, nature-based solutions, and ecosystem and environmental impact assessments.
SEL is committed to advancing water treatment, the circular economy, water reuse, and resource recovery. By combining cutting-edge science with practical applications, its interdisciplinary research contributes to the transition towards a greener and more climate-resilient future. Through its research and educational activities, SEL also supports the development of the next generation of engineers, scientists, and leaders, equipping them with the knowledge and skills required to address future environmental challenges.

entityDescription:
ATELIER ETUDE VOLTA (ADEV)
Independent power electronics design house for space, defence and scientific instrumentation
ADEV is a French SAS and an independent SME in Palaiseau, Paris-Saclay. It takes power conversion hardware from concept to characterised engineering model (TRL 1 to TRL 6) for primes, space SMEs and research infrastructures, on conventional and nanosatellite platforms, regulated and unregulated buses.

CORE COMPETENCES
High voltage power supplies: regulated 2 kV to 50 kV from 28 V to 120 V buses, analogue control loops avoiding radiation sensitive digital controllers, corona and partial discharge control, Paschen margin, low outgassing potting (ECSS-Q-ST-70-02).
Electric propulsion: PPU stages, anode, cathode heater and keeper supplies for Hall effect, FEEP and electrospray thrusters.
Spacecraft power: EPS and PCDU architectures, bus regulation, battery management, protected distribution.
DC/DC conversion and point of load: isolated and non-isolated converters from watts to kilowatts, resonant LLC and dual active bridge topologies, gallium nitride and silicon carbide power stages, gate drivers, custom magnetics, multi-rail sub-volt regulation at tens of amperes, low noise instrumentation front ends and traction inverters.

DESIGN AND CHARACTERISATION
Schematic capture, PCB layout and DfM in Altium, KiCad or customer toolchain on request. SPICE and thermal simulation, worst case and part stress analysis with derating (ECSS-Q-ST-30-11), FMEA, EEE parts selection for total ionising dose and single event effects. Laboratory in France, EMC pre-compliance (CISPR, MIL-STD-461, DO-160), thermal testing -55°C to +180°C, BGA and QFN rework.

SMALL SERIES AND QUALIFICATION
ADEV covers breadboard (BB), elegant breadboard (EBB) and engineering model (EM), and manufactures small series of non flight qualified hardware for ground support equipment, test benches and instrumentation. Hardware is architected against ECSS from the outset, so moving to flight standard needs no redesign, and delivered with a build to print package (DDF, DJF, DCL, DML, DPL). ADEV supports qualification campaigns and coordinates European partners for space grade EEE procurement, qualified assembly and accredited testing, giving one technical interlocutor through to qualified hardware. Customer intellectual property and bills of materials remain theirs.

COMPANY
Founded in 2025 by Thomas Harmand, PhD on GaN space power converters (SATIE, ENS Paris-Saclay), and Raphael Filipe, 18 years in industry, 6 in space on flight qualified DC/DC converters, 12 in automotive at Valeo and Continental. A network of independent senior specialists, all in France, adds mechanical engineering, FPGA, radiation and system engineering competences on demand, so substantial multidisciplinary projects are addressed, with design authority retained by ADEV. ADEV is open to ESA TDE, GSTP and ARTES programmes and collaborative R&D, working to SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR reviews.

entityDescription:
Marcos Aerospace I.K.E. is a Greek aerospace engineering company developing unmanned aircraft systems and space-enabled technologies for wildfire management and aerial firefighting.
Its principal programme, Quencher, is a purpose-built unmanned amphibious firefighting aircraft with a planned suppressant payload of approximately 4,500 litres. It is being developed for large-scale, day and night wildfire operations, including AI-assisted coordinated multi-aircraft missions and remotely supervised or autonomous operation, subject to the applicable regulatory and certification framework.
The concept combines GNSS, satellite communications and Earth observation data with onboard sensing and mission-management systems to support navigation, situational awareness, wildfire monitoring and mission planning. Quencher is conceived as a scalable, lower-cost firefighting system in which multiple aircraft can operate cooperatively to deliver substantial aggregate suppression capacity.

description:
microXpace is a French biotechnology SME developing microbiome-derived technologies based on the functional interactions between microorganisms, host physiology and metabolism.

Our core capabilities include microbiome and microbial-metabolism research, host–microbiome interactions, functional microbiology, omics-based analysis, biomarker and target identification, and the design and experimental validation of microbiome-derived interventions. microXpace combines scientific discovery with translational development, from mechanistic studies and proof-of-concept testing to product-oriented R&D.

Building on this expertise, microXpace is expanding its activities into Space Health and Human Spaceflight, with a particular interest in how the space environment may alter microbial functions and host–microbiome metabolic interactions, and how these changes could contribute to physiological risks during long-duration missions. Current R&D explores microbial metabolic pathways, including bile-acid metabolism, as potential targets for monitoring and for the future development of microbiome-derived countermeasures.

microXpace is interested in collaborations with research organisations, space-industry partners and technology providers in areas including space life sciences, human health, microbiome research, microbial metabolism, omics, biosensing, experimental platforms and biological payload development. We are particularly interested in research partnerships, technical collaborations, consortium participation and opportunities to adapt biotechnology developed outside the space sector to space applications.

ESYEN also operates an R&D business unit focused primarily on Artificial Intelligence and Cyber-security activities.

Its engineering capability covers the complete hardware and firmware value chain: schematic design and PCB layout, antenna engineering for GNSS and V2X (including multi-band and ground-plane-constrained designs), enclosure, thermal, vibration and IP-rated mechanical design, power management and energy-harvesting concepts, embedded Linux board support and driver development, GNSS receiver and IMU integration across multiple vendor families, GNSS and RTK / correction-service handling, sensor data acquisition and diagnostic and end-of-line test firmware. The company also covers manufacturing readiness, production test concepts and small-batch production.

cubesys is the developer of the cube:evk, an all-purpose device and development platform for V2X applications, validated across a wide range of vehicle types and infrastructure environments, and of the cube:nano compact C-ITS platform for two-wheeled vehicles, combining dual-radio V2X (ITS-G5 and C-V2X) with high-accuracy GNSS-based positioning.

Together with its parent company nfiniity GmbH, which contributes ITS software, V2X protocol stacks and system integration, cubesys forms a vertically integrated group covering hardware, firmware and software for standards-compliant connected-mobility products. Target markets include two-wheeler and vehicle manufacturers, mobility service operators, road operators and research institutions.

White Noise is an aerospace engineering research and development unit based at the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA). Operating under the supervision of the NTUA Machine Elements Laboratory, the unit focuses on the applied engineering and implementation of space technologies.
The unit's core technical capabilities encompass the complete lifecycle including research, design, manufacturing, and testing of advanced aerospace systems. Primary domains of expertise include the development of sounding rockets, CubeSats, and related suborbital flight systems. White Noise conducts applied engineering in areas such as propulsion, aerodynamics, and aerospace structures, executing complex technological projects from conceptual design through to launch operations.

entityDescription:
The Water Business Unit of Antea Group Belgium supports public authorities, utilities, industries, and infrastructure operators in addressing water-related challenges through a combination of engineering, environmental expertise, digital innovation, and data-driven solutions. The team works across the full water cycle, including water resources management, hydraulic engineering, water modelling, climate adaptation, flood and drought management, river restoration, groundwater management, and water infrastructure planning. 
Our multidisciplinary experts combine domain knowledge in hydrology, hydraulics, hydrogeology, climate resilience, and environmental management with advanced digital capabilities such as geospatial analysis, Earth Observation, numerical modelling, artificial intelligence, and decision-support tools. This integrated approach enables us to translate complex environmental and operational data into actionable insights for water managers and infrastructure owners. 
The Water Business Unit is actively involved in the development of innovative solutions for climate-resilient water systems, including river and flood modelling, drought risk assessment, water stewardship, digital water management, and satellite-enabled services. By combining technical expertise with stakeholder engagement and operational understanding, Antea Group helps clients make informed decisions and build more resilient water systems.

entityDescription:
The Fraunhofer Research Institution for Energy Infrastructures and Geotechnologies IEG carries out research in the fields of integrated energy infrastructures, geothermal energy and sector coupling for a successful energy transition at seven locations. We develop ideas, technologies and strategies for the next phase of the transformation of the energy systems and see ourselves as independent pioneers in politics, economics, regulation and society. By founding Fraunhofer IEG, the Fraunhofer Society is making a significant contribution to exploiting the markets in a more targeted way for the use of geothermal energy systems, the storage of energy sources and technologies to couple the energy sectors of heat, electricity and transportation.
Our expertise in the field of energy research is based on the synergy of our employees’ technical, natural science and economic knowledge.
In our work, we not only use a wide range of advanced scientific methods and models based on our extensive experimental laboratory and testing infrastructure, we also develop these continuously using knowledge obtained from the research projects we have carried out.

entityDescription:
Siora is an Earth Observation and AI company developing satellite-based soil and crop intelligence solutions for agriculture.
Our core soil intelligence solution provides field-level estimates of parameters including nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH, soil organic matter, cation exchange capacity (CEC), soil texture and other physical soil properties. The resulting spatial maps can be used to identify variability within fields, support fertilisation planning, create management zones and enable variable-rate applications.

Our technology transforms satellite imagery and other geospatial data into actionable information about agricultural fields. By combining Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations with terrain, climate, geological and other environmental data, together with machine learning models, Siora can estimate key soil characteristics at high spatial resolution without requiring extensive physical soil sampling.
In addition to soil analysis, Siora develops Earth Observation tools for continuous agricultural monitoring, including vegetation condition, water stress and moisture-related indicators. Our objective is to turn complex remote sensing data into information that farmers, agronomists and agricultural companies can use directly in operational decision-making.
The platform is designed to provide analysis rapidly and at scale, from individual agricultural fields to large farming portfolios. Results can be delivered through Siora's web platform as well as through standard geospatial and data formats for integration into other farm management and precision agriculture systems.
Siora is particularly interested in collaboration and R&D projects involving Earth Observation, precision agriculture, soil monitoring and mapping, sustainable fertilisation, variable-rate application, crop and vegetation monitoring, water stress, climate-smart agriculture, land management and the development of new downstream applications of satellite data.
We are open to participating in ESA and European collaborative projects as a technology provider, Earth Observation data analytics partner, AI/ML partner, agricultural use-case provider or pilot and validation partner.
